text:
Ryan: ran a quick nsys on the failing workload, looks like the kernel timeline drifts ~20-30ms per-request after the batching changes. attaching snippets from the timeline.
Marta: ah, is that the new dynamic-batch-size heuristic you landed yesterday?
Ryan: yeah. it changed the sequencing of kernels, and when we shove NVTX ranges around kernels it pushes the visible start times in the perf timeline. not sure if it's real latency or just annotation overhead.
Sanjay: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to repro locally.
Ryan: `nsys profile -o trace --trace=cuda,osrt,stack --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --stop-on-exit python serve_bench.py`
Emily: fwiw NVTX ranges are cheap but not free. if you're adding very fine-grained ranges per microkernel we might be adding syscall/kernel traffic that perturb the scheduler.
Marta: we already wrap each cudaLaunch with nvtxRangePush/pop in runtime/kernels.cpp. we did it to get per-kernel names for perfetto.
Sanjay: two options: keep the fine-grained ranges but switch to sampled-span mode in traces (reduce frequency) OR move to coarse per-request spans plus local micro-span counters (no NVTX).
Ryan: i tried sampled traces (`--sample=cpu`) and the drift reduced but hotspots are less obvious. we need a naming scheme for coarse spans that still maps back to kernel indices.
Emily: proposal: per-request span named `req:<short-hash>` from entry->exit. Inside, annotate kernel events with `K{seq}:{arch}:{kernel-kind}` but use in-memory mapping rather than nvtx for each kernel. Only emit a single NVTX with a blob id that maps to the recorded kernel list in the profiler artifact.
Marta: so NVTX payload = span id; kernel list captured in our debug dump. that would avoid syscall per kernel. how to implement quickly?
Sanjay: sketch: maintain thread_local vector<KernelDesc> cur_span_kernels; on kernel_launch push descriptor (name, op, duration_hint); only nvtxPush at span start with `nvtxNameCategoryA(0, span_id)` and nvtxRangePop at span end. after trace, we materialize kernel timeline by combining span_id + cur_span_kernels from logs.
Ryan: nice. code sketch:
```
thread_local std::vector<KernelDesc>* g_active_kernels = nullptr;
void span_start(uint64_t id){ if(!g_active_kernels) g_active_kernels = new ...; g_active_kernels->clear(); nvtxMarkA(id); }
void kernel_launched(const KernelDesc &k){ if(g_active_kernels) g_active_kernels->push_back(k); }
void span_end(){ nvtxMarkA(0); /* write out g_active_kernels to tmp file */ }
```
Emily: prefer nvtxMark over push/pop to avoid range nesting overhead. Mark+external mapping keeps perf timelines light.
kevin-ci: perf-bot ran replay job 19187-a and shows KV cache prefetches increase when we coalesce batches differently — could be causing more small kernels which increases annotation frequency.
Marta: that fits: dynamic batching sometimes splits large requests and triggers extra KV reads. we should bias the heuristic to avoid tiny micro-batches below 4 tokens unless latency SLO requires it.
Sanjay: also check kernel selection fallback code; if kernel-selector swaps to small-block kernels on certain sequence lengths we get many more launches. adding a single merged-range per selector decision point might help.
Ryan: action items:
- Marta: prototype span-id + kernel-list mapping approach, minimize NVTX calls (ETA EOD)
- Emily: validate nvtxMark vs push/pop overhead with a microbench (nsys and perfetto) (ETA tomorrow)
- Sanjay: update batching heuristic to avoid micro-batches in bench profile and re-run nsys (ETA today)
- kevin-ci: run the perf-bot sweep with the new sampling flags and KV metrics (ETA next)
Marta: ack. i'll also add a fallback flag so we can A/B revert the instrumentation.
kevin-ci: perf-bot: scheduled nightly trace with `nsys profile --sample=none` + perfetto capture. will post artifacts.
perf-bot: uploaded /artifacts/1918765432/nsys_trace.qdrep and /artifacts/1918765432/kernel_dump.json
Ryan: i'll parse the kernel_dump.json and try to overlay timestamps to verify whether drift is real or annotation-only. if annotation-only we can keep the fine-grained view behind an env var.
Emily: if we keep opt-in fine spans, add clear naming conventions: `K:<op>:<impl>:v{major}` and avoid long human text. tools can map op->readable name.
Sanjay: one more: for perfetto, we can emit perfetto counters for KV cache hits/misses per span_id so we can correlate cache churn to kernel-density.
Marta: good idea. i'll add a small ring-buffer to push KV events keyed by span_id so perf-bot can ingest them.
Ryan: thanks all — posting repro steps and a short checklist when the artifacts are up. :thumbsup:
